task.description: Implement REQ-036 per the validated design at lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md (PASS from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR). Verify branch first: git branch --show-current must equal feature/WF02-REQ036-20260817. Implement exactly the 3 modules the design specifies -- lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_plan.ex (Letflow.Definitions.PromotionPlan.compute_promotion_plan/5), lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_conflict.ex (Letflow.Definitions.PromotionConflict.reject_if_conflicts/4), lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest.ex (Letflow.Definitions.PromotionDigest.compute_plan_digest/1 + verify_digest/2). Follow the design's algorithm steps, type shapes, error atoms, and named helper functions (canonicalize/1, version_greater?/2, default_tenant_classifier/1, default permission_checker with NO enforcement) exactly -- this design already passed a hard validation gate, do not silently diverge from it. If you find a genuine reason to diverge, state it explicitly in your handoff's issues, do not just change it quietly. No migration needed (process_definitions already exists per REQ-027). No writes -- all 3 modules are pure/read-only, matching INV-PRM-1 through INV-PRM-5 in the design's Section 8 (grep for Repo.insert/update/delete/update_all across all 3 files must return zero hits when you're done). Every moduledoc must restate: PromotionPlan's permission_checker has no real enforcement by default (per design 9.1); PromotionDigest's verify_digest/2 uses :crypto.hash_equals/2, not ==/=:=, explicitly per AC6.
acceptance_criteria: MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test still passes (baseline, no regressions -- new tests come from TEST-DESIGNER in Step 3, but nothing here should break existing tests)
No SQL string interpolation of tenant/user data (Repo.get_by/3 with prefix: only, matching the design's DB access pattern)
Zero Repo.insert/update/delete/update_all calls across all 3 new files (read-only invariant)
All 3 modules' public function signatures match the validated design exactly (name, arity, @spec)
Every new public function has a one-line @doc; moduledocs restate the two flagged behavioural notes (permission_checker has no real enforcement by default; verify_digest/2 uses :crypto.hash_equals/2)

result.summary: Implemented all 3 modules per the validated design (lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md): Letflow.Definitions.PromotionPlan.compute_promotion_plan/5, Letflow.Definitions.PromotionConflict.reject_if_conflicts/4, Letflow.Definitions.PromotionDigest.compute_plan_digest/1 + verify_digest/2. All read-only/pure -- zero Repo.insert/update/delete/update_all calls across the 3 files (grep-verified). mix compile --warnings-as-errors exits 0, mix format --check-formatted exits 0, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test passes 4 properties/467 tests/0 failures (no regressions). Ad hoc pure smoke test of PromotionDigest confirmed AC5 (key-order-independent digest determinism) and verify_digest/2's constant-time behavior against both a direct digest string and a plan map. Both moduledoc-restatement requirements are in place: PromotionPlan's moduledoc states permission_checker has no real enforcement by default (design 9.1) and default_permission_checker/2's own @doc restates it; PromotionDigest's moduledoc and verify_digest/2's @doc state :crypto.hash_equals/2 is the only comparator, never ==/=:=.

issues.description: Design 9.1 says opts[:permission_checker] 'has no built-in default' but leaves unstated what happens if a caller omits it entirely. This implementation resolves that gap explicitly (not silently): compute_promotion_plan/5 uses Keyword.fetch!(opts, :permission_checker), which raises KeyError if the caller omits the option, rather than silently defaulting to allow-all or deny-all. default_permission_checker/2 is implemented as a named reference function per the design's suggestion, but is deliberately NOT wired in as the automatic Keyword.get fallback (doing so would silently grant real-looking-but-fake enforcement) -- it is exposed only as an explicit opt-in a caller can pass. Flagging for REVIEWER to confirm this resolution of the design's own open gap is acceptable.

PromotionConflict.reject_if_conflicts/4's @type conflict_error and reject_if_conflicts/4's mismatched-length short-circuit are implemented as a separate function head with an `when length(process_key) != length(base_version)` guard (returning {:error, :mismatched_process_key_list} before any tenant/DB work), rather than as a first step inside a single function body -- functionally identical to the design's numbered algorithm (§4.2 step 1) but structured as idiomatic Elixir multiple-clause dispatch. No behavioral divergence, noting the stylistic choice for REVIEWER.
